- When sentiment is positive (≥0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.25), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially in early horizon.
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the 10–15 day horizon after recent spikes; add 2–5% buffer to forecast.
- Model overestimates in the 20+ day horizon after calm periods; apply downward correction of 3–7%.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, forecast should not continue falling; pivot upward.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00) and price is rising, model often fails to capture momentum; add 1–3% lagged momentum boost.
- Overshoot after spikes: if model peaks 5–10% above true peak, reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 3–5 days.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are prone to overconfidence; apply 2–5% downward adjustment if sentiment is flat or negative.
